# Prioritize

Turns Triage into an ordered Todo queue. The order comes from what each issue needs and what the code looks like today, and it is recorded in the issue **Relationships** (blocked by / blocking), which you read **and write**. Reuses `/triage` for labels and agent briefs. Rubrics and the comment template: [RUBRICS.md](RUBRICS.md). The scripts use GraphQL and few requests (one read, one write): pass several issues to one call, and use `apply` for per-issue fields.

Every comment must start with: `> *This was generated by AI during triage.*`

```bash
Q=~/.claude/skills/prioritize/scripts/queue.sh
B=~/.claude/skills/project-board/scripts/board.sh
R=~/.claude/skills/project-board/scripts/blockers.sh
```

## 1. Read the queue

`$Q` returns JSON: the issues in Triage and Todo in board order, top first (issues further along the board, e.g. Done, are not listed; they only show up as blockers) (number, title, `column`, labels, `hasAcceptance`, `ranked`, `blockedBy` with each blocker's `state` and board `status`, `blocking`). With no board (`board: null`) it returns all open issues; skip those with `ranked: true` (already ranked; `ranked` is always false with a board). The repo must have one linked board or none.

## 2. Understand each issue and the code

Claim the Triage issues you work on: `$B claim Triager <n> <n> ...`. Read each issue and its comments (`gh issue view <n> --json title,body,labels,comments`; `--comments` prints nothing in a non-interactive shell, and `gh issue view` takes one issue per call), `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` if present, then explore the code with Grep, Glob and Read, and `git log` for recent work. Go through the checklist in RUBRICS.md. Write down per issue: what exists already, what it touches, what it needs from other issues. If the code shows the issue is already implemented, do not queue it: leave it in Triage, comment where you found it and recommend closing it in the report (you cannot close issues).

## 3. Fix the relationships

The Relationships are the model of the order, so make them right before ranking:

- Add a missing blocker: `$R add <n> <blocker>` when `<n>` needs something the blocker creates, or both change the same code.
- Remove a wrong one: `$R remove <n> <blocker>` only when clearly unnecessary; when in doubt leave it. Name every removed blocker (number and title) in the comment so it can be restored.
- Explain every change in the issue comment. `$R list <n>` shows the result; `add` refuses a self-link and a direct cycle with an error: do not retry or force it, report it. Check longer cycles yourself.

## 4. Check readiness, set Priority, Size, Estimate

**Ready** = a clear description, acceptance criteria and none of the repo's `needs-info`, `wontfix` or duplicate labels (the label names come from the repo's triage label mapping, `docs/agents/triage-labels.md` created by `/setup-skills`; the defaults are `needs-info`, `wontfix`, `duplicate`). Not ready: stays in Triage, add the repo's `needs-info` label (create it first if missing), comment what is missing, point to `/triage`. Size XL: stays in Triage, recommend splitting with `/to-issues`.

Choose Priority, Size and Estimate with RUBRICS.md. Issues already in Todo keep their values unless empty.

## 5. Order

Let **S** be the ready Triage issues plus the issues already in Todo.

1. A blocker outside S is **settled** when it is closed, or its column is Done, Doing, Review or Testing. An open blocker that is not on the board, not ready, XL or left in Triage is not settled.
2. Fill the places one at a time. An issue may take the next place only when every blocker is settled or already placed. Among those pick by: higher Priority, then the one that blocks more issues, then smaller Size, then lower number. So a blocker in Todo always comes before its dependents.
3. An issue that never gets a place (unsettled blocker, cycle) is not queued. A Triage issue stays in Triage; one already in Todo goes back (`$B move <n> triage`). Say why in its comment and in the report.

## 6. Queue in order

Queue all placed Triage issues with **one call**: a plan on stdin, one issue per line, fields separated by `|` (setting the Status also clears your claim). Add lines with `--if-empty` to fill empty values of issues already in Todo:

```bash
$B apply <<'PLAN'
4|Status=Todo|Priority=P0|Size=M|Estimate=6
5|Status=Todo|Priority=P0|Size=M|Estimate=6
7|Priority=P1|Size=S|Estimate=3|--if-empty
PLAN
```

Release the claims of the issues you left in Triage: `$B release <n> ...`. Then put the whole queue in rank order with one call, existing Todo issues included: `$B order <n1> <n2> <n3> ...` (first = top, the coder takes the top). Check with `$Q` that Todo shows that order. Post the comments (RUBRICS.md; when you re-rank an issue that already has a `Queue position:` comment, start the new one with the line `Re-ranked, supersedes the earlier queue comment.`); `N` in `Queue position: #k of N` is the number of issues in the final queue (placed ones only).

## No board

The same commands run and print `SKIPPED` for the board parts (`order` too). Study, fix relationships and rank, set and move nothing, and add `(no board, nothing moved)` to each comment. The handover is manual.

## Report

End with a table: order, issue, Priority, Size, relationships changed, and the reason for every issue left in Triage or moved back.
